issue.title: desktop-weekly: report fixes, wider Jetson eviction and host load sampling
issue.body:
## What

- `report.py`: the cross-backend speed table indexed a row for every backend; a cell that is not expected (a Metal-only family, or a `family:backend` skip from #421) now renders as `n/a`, and a family with no row at all in the run (Metal-only families on a CPU-only run) is left out instead of raising StopIteration.
- `lib.sh`: the per-cell page-cache eviction (`EVICT_PAGE_CACHE=1`, Jetson) now covers the build, source and dependency trees as well as the model store; the example config lists the eight Jetson cells that exceed its CUDA and Vulkan heaps.
- Host load sampling: before each cell the driver records the share of the CPUs busy over one second and the one-minute load average into `<family>.load.json`; `summarize.py` flags the cell as contended at 10% busy or more and lists it under problems, the report shows `ok (under load)`, the dashboard rows carry the flag and a caveat with a commentary item per task, and the task pages mark the bar.

## Why

The first scheduled run (2026-11-08) finished its cells on every host, but `report.py` raised `KeyError: ('cpu', 'parakeet-mlx')` on the Mac Studio and `KeyError: ('cuda', 'nemotron-abcba')` on the Jetson, so both runs ended with a FAILED marker although their results were complete; the Mac Studio's CPU-lane rerun then hit the StopIteration. The reports were rebuilt by hand with these fixes.

The Jetson run rebuilt three backends before benchmarking and then lost two Vulkan cells to allocations that had passed in Friday's rehearsal (which ran with `--no-update`); the fresh build artefacts sit in the page cache, which the NVIDIA allocator does not reclaim, so they are evicted too (0.2 s per cell). Two Vulkan cells still exceed the Tegra Vulkan heap with the cache evicted and are skipped per backend.

The Mac Studio CPU lane ran 3-200x slower on Sunday than on Friday and timed seven cells out while another user's work kept the shared machine busy; the same build on the idle machine matched Friday. Nothing in the data showed that, hence the load sample.

## Tests

- `test_report.py`: `n/a` for a family expected on one backend only; a family without any row is left out; a contended row says `ok (under load)`.
- `test_summarize.py`: a cell sampled at 35% busy is flagged and listed, one at 3% is not, and the run status stays ok.
- `test_build_dashboard_data.py` and `test_task_views.py`: the flag, the caveat, the commentary items and the bar label.
- `test-desktop-weekly.sh`: the eviction covers the model store and the build, source and dependency trees; the busy-share arithmetic for /proc/stat ticks and the macOS `top` line; `write_host_load` writes numbers; `discard_cell` drops the sample (30 checks pass).

issue.title: fix(parakeet): link test-encoder-device-decode in shared-library builds
issue.body:
## Summary

`test-encoder-device-decode` (from #402) fails to link in every build where `qvac-parakeet` is a shared library: the test calls internal entry points (`run_encoder`, `tdt_prepare_runtime`, `tdt_greedy_decode`, `resolve_nemotron_prompt_id`, the Nemotron prompt projections, `load_from_gguf`) that the library hides (`CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET hidden`). The parakeet CI lanes build the library static, so they pass; the whisper CI umbrella lanes (`umbrella (ubuntu-24.04)`, `umbrella (macos-14)`, `umbrella-webgpu`) build it shared and fail with `undefined reference to parakeet::...`. Those lanes only trigger on whisper paths, so master has not built the target since #402; they showed up on #390, which touches `whisper-ci.yml`.

The fix compiles the parakeet sources into the test directly, with the same source list, link set and include directories as `test-encoder-graph-cache`, the pattern the file already uses for tests of non-exported entry points (`test-rnnt`, `test-tdt-decoder-parity`).

## Test plan

- [x] Umbrella configuration (`cmake -S . -B build -DSPEECH_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<ggml-install>`, shared `libqvac-parakeet.so`): `test-encoder-device-decode` builds and links
- [x] whisper CI umbrella lanes green on this branch: the workflow does not trigger on parakeet paths, so it was dispatched by hand as [run 42644214521](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-fabric-speech.cpp/actions/runs/42644214521); `umbrella (ubuntu-24.04)`, `umbrella (macos-14)`, `umbrella-webgpu` and `model-conversion` all pass
- [x] parakeet CI (static library) unchanged: the PR's own lanes are green

issue.title: ggml : add ROPE_FLUX (CPU, Vulkan, Metal)
issue.body:
## Overview

Ports `ROPE_FLUX`, the fused Flux RoPE from diffusion GGML, into fabric's GGML. It rotates every (even, odd) pair of a `[d_head, n_head, L, N]` tensor by a precomputed 2x2 matrix and writes the result in the `[d_head, L, N*n_head]` layout flash attention takes. A NULL matrix gives the permute alone.

```c
struct ggml_tensor * ggml_rope_flux(struct ggml_context * ctx, struct ggml_tensor * a, struct ggml_tensor * b);
```

`b` is `[2, 2, d_head/2, L]`, and `b[i, j]` multiplies input component `i` into output component `j`.

## Commits

| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| `ggml : add the ROPE_FLUX op with a CPU reference` | Op appended after the base's ragged ops (`GGML_OP_COUNT` 132, RPC protocol 117 after the merge with `temp-11739`), CPU kernel, `tests/test-rope-flux.cpp` (closed-form oracle), 9 `test-backend-ops` cases, docs |
| `vulkan : add ROPE_FLUX` | `rope_flux.comp` imported unchanged; the F32 view addressability helper is now shared with `CONVROT` and loses its ConvRot name |
| `metal : add ROPE_FLUX` | Rotation and permute-only kernels in the rope library; outputs above `INT32_MAX` elements are declined |

CUDA has no kernel, as in diffusion, and declines the op in `supports_op`. Stable-diffusion checks `ggml_backend_supports_op` at every `ggml_rope_flux` call site and builds the unfused RoPE (mul, add, permute, cont) instead, so on CUDA the rotation stays on the GPU.

## Provenance

Source: tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml `2026-08-11` at `a4adfcb1`.

- Core and CPU: `481ebd1b`, `1a9e1ad9`, `563b89e5`
- Vulkan: `b4c8ce43` (the shader is byte-identical)
- Metal: `481ebd1b`, `a982fe1c`, `1a9e1ad9`, `22f4bfc2`

Fabric-specific: the op sits at the end of the enum, the CPU kernel is split into small helpers, the Metal kernels go into `kernels/rope.metal` rather than one monolithic file, and the Vulkan host code uses a push-constant struct.

## Validation

- CPU: `test-rope-flux` 4/4 (rotation and permute-only, contiguous and strided input), `test-backend-ops -o ROPE_FLUX` 9/9.
- Vulkan: 9/9 on RTX 5090 and on the RADV iGPU, no messages under `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`. `CONVROT` 22/22 and `MUL_MAT_CONVROT` 18/18 and 20/20 still pass after the helper rename.
- CUDA: reports the op as unsupported; `MUL_MAT_CONVROT` 24/24 unchanged.
- RPC: `test-rpc-local` passes at protocol 117.

## Not covered

- **Metal is not run locally.** The Mac hosts were unreachable, so the Metal kernels rely on CI's `gpu-metal` job, and their `docs/ops/Metal.csv` rows were written by analogy with the CPU rows.
- No case crosses Vulkan's first workgroup dimension limit (that needs over 33M output elements); the dispatch splits it into a second dimension the same way as `CONVROT`.

> [medium] ggml/src/ggml.c — line 4967 (GGML_ASSERT(a->ne[1] <= INT64_MAX / a->ne[3]);)
> 
> > A valid empty batch such as ggml_new_tensor_4d(ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32, 8, 3, 5, 0) reaches this assertion and divides by zero during graph construction. GGML permits zero dimensions, and the new API has no nonempty precondition. Guard the division when a->ne[3] == 0 and add a zero-batch constructor test.

Fixed in f9d0384a3. The overflow check is now GGML_ASSERT(a->ne[3] == 0 || a->ne[1] <= INT64_MAX / a->ne[3]);, so an empty batch builds a [d_head, L, 0, 1] result without dividing. At compute time, the CPU, Vulkan and Metal backends already skip empty nodes. test-rope-flux gains two cases, “rotate empty batch” and “permute only empty batch”. Each builds a [8, 3, 5, 0] input, with and without pe, computes the graph and checks for an empty, contiguous [8, 5, 0, 1] output. With the guard reverted, the test crashes before it prints anything. With the fix, all 6 cases pass.

Ports ConvRot from the diffusion GGML (tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml `2026-08-11`) into fabric's `ggml/`, ahead of the full diffusion merge. It also brings the `GGML_PREC_F32` precision fixes that ConvRot's Vulkan GEMM path relies on.

ConvRot is the ComfyUI TensorWise I8 weight format: int8 weights with a per-output-row F32 scale, whose input dimension is rotated in groups by the regular radix-4 Hadamard transform.

There are five commits, and each one builds and passes on its own:

1. **`ggml : add the ConvRot ops with a CPU reference`**
   - Adds `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_CONVROT`, `GGML_OP_CONVROT`, `GGML_HINT_SRC0_IS_CONVROT_H256` and `ggml_convrot_repack_q8_0`.
   - Bumps the RPC protocol major. It is 115 after merging `temp-11739`, which took 114 for F8_E4M3.
   - Adds test-backend-ops cases and a new `test-convrot`, which checks every backend against closed-form oracles.
2. **`cuda : add ConvRot and the native H256 transform`**
3. **`vulkan, metal, cuda : honor GGML_PREC_F32 on F32 x F32 matmuls`**
   - Before this commit, an F32 x F32 `MUL_MAT` that asked for F32 lost precision on all three GPU backends:
     - Vulkan staged the operands in F16.
     - Metal's simdgroup `mul_mm` staged them in half.
     - CUDA ran MMF and cuBLAS in TF32.
   - Each backend now takes a full-F32 path for these matmuls, which is slower but keeps the precision. After review, that path is keyed on the src1 operand precision (`ggml_prec_set_src(t, GGML_PREC_F32, 1)`) rather than the accumulator flag, so the KQ matmul without flash attention, which only sets the accumulator flag, keeps its fast kernels.
   - Default-precision matmuls and other weight types are unchanged.
   - The new `test_mul_mat_prec_f32` holds six cases to an NMSE of 1e-9.
4. **`vulkan : add ConvRot`**
5. **`metal : add ConvRot`**

Follow-up commits from review and CI:

6. **`ci, tests : stabilize the ConvRot checks on macOS`**
   - Drops the flaky single-output f16-compat case. It failed about one run in 40 on Metal, because NMSE over one value blows up near zero.
   - Skips test-convrot on the paravirtual macOS runner, as that job already does for the other GPU correctness tests.
7. **`vulkan, metal, cuda : key full-F32 matmuls on the src1 operand precision`**
8. **`vulkan : reject misaligned MUL_MAT_CONVROT views`**, with a regression test.
9. **`rpc : keep CONVROT off RPC devices too`**, with a test-rpc check.
10. **`vulkan : size the staged B column stride by the staged type`**
    - A full-F32 matmul stages a strided src1 as F32, but the chunked dispatch used an F16 column stride.
    - A new PREC_F32 case with N = 2105344 failed on RADV before the fix.

## Additional information

**Testing.** Every commit was built and tested on its own. The final tree:

| Backend | MUL_MAT (includes prec=f32) | MUL_MAT_CONVROT | CONVROT | test-convrot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA (RTX 5090, CUDA 13.3) | 3429/3429 | 24/24 | not supported | pass |
| Vulkan (RTX 5090 and RADV Raphael iGPU) | 3260/3260 each | 20/20 each | 22/22 each | pass |
| Metal (M3 Ultra) | 3386/3386 | 24/24 | 22/22 | pass |
| CPU | reference | reference | reference | pass |

The `MUL_MAT_CONVROT_H256` cases pass (3/3) everywhere. Without the CUDA change in commit 3, the new 16-column PREC_F32 case fails on CUDA at 4.65e-7.

**Not tested.** The gfx1151-only Vulkan path, because the Strix hosts were busy.

**After the follow-up commits:**
- **CUDA:** MUL_MAT 3429/3429, MUL_MAT_CONVROT 24/24.
- **Vulkan:**
  - MUL_MAT 3260/3260 on each device.
  - MUL_MAT_CONVROT 20/20 on RADV; 18/18 on NVIDIA, which now rejects the two misaligned-view cases.
- **Metal:** MUL_MAT 3386/3386 and MUL_MAT_CONVROT 24/24 on both M3 Ultra and M4.
- **RPC:** `test-rpc-local` passes, and fails without the RPC change.

**Carried over unchanged from the diffusion branch.** These are left as they are so the later full diffusion merge stays clean. They are worth fixing there:
- **CUDA:**
  - CUDA has no `GGML_OP_CONVROT`, so the rotation runs on another backend.
  - The batched native `MUL_MAT_CONVROT` path is an I8 dot-product kernel that does not use tensor cores.
- **f16-compat:** the mode behaves differently per backend:
  - CUDA accumulates in F16.
  - Metal and Vulkan accumulate in F32.
  - CPU ignores the flag.
- **Vulkan:** the gfx1151 split path drains the GPU queue and reads a range flag back to the host on every call.

**Not ported from tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml#68.** That PR also stops quantized weights from using MMQ/MMVQ under `GGML_PREC_F32`. I left that part out. llama.cpp sets `GGML_PREC_F32` on the GLM4 FFN and on the KQ matmul when flash attention is off, so it would slow those matmuls down in fabric.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. Claude Code:
  - ported the code from the diffusion branch and wrote the fabric integration and the CUDA precision fix;
  - built and tested on all four backends and ran a self-review;
  - split the work into commits and drafted the commit messages and this description.

> Most of the ConvRot implementation here is already covered by [qvac-ext-ggml #88](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml/pull/88) and its follow-ups, with the diffusion-side loading and dispatch integration in [qvac-ext-stable-diffusion.cpp #41](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-stable-diffusion.cpp/pull/41) (that PR itself is still open). This PR is useful as a port into fabric's vendored GGML, as its description acknowledges.
> 
> Could we pin the source diffusion GGML commit and clearly separate the imported implementation from the fabric-specific changes? The operand-precision handling, Vulkan alignment/stride fixes and RPC fixes are the interesting additional work. We should assess those for backporting into qvac-ext-ggml where applicable, so the two copies stay aligned ahead of the full merge.
> 
> The inline notes identify those boundaries and follow-up opportunities; they are not requests to reimplement the existing kernels. This review is based on the patches and source comparison; I have not independently rerun the reported GPU tests.

Thanks. I pinned the source and separated the two in 872ecc7df. It's an empty commit, and its message is the provenance record:

- **Source:** qvac-ext-ggml `2026-08-11` at `a4adfcb1`.
  - ConvRot is `7d9ce11c..9a7d2b36` (#88, #91, #93, #94).
  - The F32 precision port follows `eeda3037`, `4c84fb44` and `36e4c256`, plus the F32 part of #68 for CUDA.
- **Imported unchanged:** the nine Vulkan ConvRot shaders.
- **Imported and adapted:** the CUDA and Metal kernels, the op definitions, the CPU reference, the dispatch and the tests.
- **Fabric-specific:**
  - f68a13e9f: src1 operand precision
  - 0efedcd06: device view alignment
  - 69d377e3e: RPC also declines CONVROT
  - 3f5c36910: staged B stride
  - 5a9776707: macOS CI
  - plus the small fixes folded into the port commits
- **Backports, checked against `a4adfcb1`:**
  - The alignment and RPC fixes apply as-is.
  - The precision key first needs fabric's `ggml_prec_set_src` in diffusion.
  - The stride fix doesn't apply until diffusion gets fabric's column-windowed dispatch.

> **aegioscy** on `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:20188`:
> Good to include the device's view-alignment requirement in addition to the shader's four-byte access requirement. This review fix should be tracked for the diffusion backend too, with the offset-view regression: a four-byte-aligned view can still violate a device's larger storage-buffer alignment. This is an additional capability-check fix, separate from the imported kernel.

Assessed in 872ecc7df: this applies to qvac-ext-ggml as-is. At `a4adfcb1`, its MUL_MAT_CONVROT check only tests the four views for four-byte alignment. An offset view that breaks the device's storage-buffer alignment therefore still passes. The fix and the offset-view regression are listed as a backport candidate.

> **aegioscy** on `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:2315`:
> This is a useful distinction from a straight port: full-F32 routing is keyed on explicit src1 operand precision, preserving the fast path when callers request only F32 accumulation. Could we track the corresponding CUDA/Metal/Vulkan changes for backport assessment in qvac-ext-ggml, keeping that narrower contract? Copying the broader quantized MMQ/MMVQ restrictions from #68 would change the performance behavior discussed in this PR.

Tracked in the backport assessment in 872ecc7df. The narrower contract can't move to qvac-ext-ggml by itself yet:

- Diffusion GGML only has `ggml_mul_mat_set_prec`. That writes `op_params[0]`, its only precision field, so full F32 is keyed on it.
- The backport first needs fabric's `ggml_prec_set_src` (`op_params[3]`).
- After that, the stable-diffusion callers that rely on PREC_F32 must also set the src1 precision.

The record also notes that #68's MMQ/MMVQ restriction for quantized weights stays out.

issue.body:
## Overview

Ports ConvRot from the diffusion GGML (tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml `2026-08-11`) into fabric's `ggml/`, ahead of the full diffusion merge. It also brings the `GGML_PREC_F32` precision fixes that ConvRot's Vulkan GEMM path relies on.

ConvRot is the ComfyUI TensorWise I8 weight format: int8 weights with a per-output-row F32 scale, whose input dimension is rotated in groups by the regular radix-4 Hadamard transform.

There are five commits, and each one builds and passes on its own:

1. **`ggml : add the ConvRot ops with a CPU reference`**
   - Adds `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_CONVROT`, `GGML_OP_CONVROT`, `GGML_HINT_SRC0_IS_CONVROT_H256` and `ggml_convrot_repack_q8_0`.
   - Bumps the RPC protocol major. It is 115 after merging `temp-11739`, which took 114 for F8_E4M3.
   - Adds test-backend-ops cases and a new `test-convrot`, which checks every backend against closed-form oracles.
2. **`cuda : add ConvRot and the native H256 transform`**
3. **`vulkan, metal, cuda : honor GGML_PREC_F32 on F32 x F32 matmuls`**
   - Before this commit, an F32 x F32 `MUL_MAT` that asked for F32 lost precision on all three GPU backends:
     - Vulkan staged the operands in F16.
     - Metal's simdgroup `mul_mm` staged them in half.
     - CUDA ran MMF and cuBLAS in TF32.
   - Each backend now takes a full-F32 path for these matmuls, which is slower but keeps the precision. After review, that path is keyed on the src1 operand precision (`ggml_prec_set_src(t, GGML_PREC_F32, 1)`) rather than the accumulator flag, so the KQ matmul without flash attention, which only sets the accumulator flag, keeps its fast kernels.
   - Default-precision matmuls and other weight types are unchanged.
   - The new `test_mul_mat_prec_f32` holds six cases to an NMSE of 1e-9.
4. **`vulkan : add ConvRot`**
5. **`metal : add ConvRot`**

Follow-up commits from review and CI:

6. **`ci, tests : stabilize the ConvRot checks on macOS`**
   - Drops the flaky single-output f16-compat case. It failed about one run in 40 on Metal, because NMSE over one value blows up near zero.
   - Skips test-convrot on the paravirtual macOS runner, as that job already does for the other GPU correctness tests.
7. **`vulkan, metal, cuda : key full-F32 matmuls on the src1 operand precision`**
8. **`vulkan : reject misaligned MUL_MAT_CONVROT views`**, with a regression test.
9. **`rpc : keep CONVROT off RPC devices too`**, with a test-rpc check.
10. **`vulkan : size the staged B column stride by the staged type`**
    - A full-F32 matmul stages a strided src1 as F32, but the chunked dispatch used an F16 column stride.
    - A new PREC_F32 case with N = 2105344 failed on RADV before the fix.

## Additional information

**Testing.** Every commit was built and tested on its own. The final tree:

| Backend | MUL_MAT (includes prec=f32) | MUL_MAT_CONVROT | CONVROT | test-convrot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA (RTX 5090, CUDA 13.3) | 3429/3429 | 24/24 | not supported | pass |
| Vulkan (RTX 5090 and RADV Raphael iGPU) | 3260/3260 each | 20/20 each | 22/22 each | pass |
| Metal (M3 Ultra) | 3386/3386 | 24/24 | 22/22 | pass |
| CPU | reference | reference | reference | pass |

The `MUL_MAT_CONVROT_H256` cases pass (3/3) everywhere. Without the CUDA change in commit 3, the new 16-column PREC_F32 case fails on CUDA at 4.65e-7.

**Not tested.** The gfx1151-only Vulkan path, because the Strix hosts were busy.

**After the follow-up commits:**
- **CUDA:** MUL_MAT 3429/3429, MUL_MAT_CONVROT 24/24.
- **Vulkan:**
  - MUL_MAT 3260/3260 on each device.
  - MUL_MAT_CONVROT 20/20 on RADV; 18/18 on NVIDIA, which now rejects the two misaligned-view cases.
- **Metal:** MUL_MAT 3386/3386 and MUL_MAT_CONVROT 24/24 on both M3 Ultra and M4.
- **RPC:** `test-rpc-local` passes, and fails without the RPC change.

**Carried over unchanged from the diffusion branch.** These are left as they are so the later full diffusion merge stays clean. They are worth fixing there:
- **CUDA:**
  - CUDA has no `GGML_OP_CONVROT`, so the rotation runs on another backend.
  - The batched native `MUL_MAT_CONVROT` path is an I8 dot-product kernel that does not use tensor cores.
- **f16-compat:** the mode behaves differently per backend:
  - CUDA accumulates in F16.
  - Metal and Vulkan accumulate in F32.
  - CPU ignores the flag.
- **Vulkan:** the gfx1151 split path drains the GPU queue and reads a range flag back to the host on every call.

issue.title: QVAC-27853 fix(vulkan): destroy devices and instance before driver unload
issue.body:
## Summary

- Destroy every Vulkan device and the instance from an `atexit` handler registered after the instance and each device are created, so it runs before the driver's own exit handlers.
- Split the `vk_device_struct` destructor into an idempotent `shutdown()` that waits for the device to go idle, skips a device that was never created, and destroys the VMA allocator only when it holds no allocations.
- After the teardown, buffers, pinned host memory and backend contexts freed later by the application skip their Vulkan calls.
- New `test-vulkan-teardown`: initialise `Vulkan0`, allocate and free a buffer, exit; a second ctest entry exits with the buffer still allocated.

## Error corrected

On the Jetson Orin (L4T 36.4, NVIDIA Tegra Vulkan driver 540.4.0, `nvgpu`), the speech CLIs finished their work, wrote their results, and then died with SIGSEGV at exit. The weekly bench therefore recorded 5 of the Jetson's 13 Vulkan cells as failed although their measurements were complete. Affected: Parakeet TDT, Parakeet Unified, Audio8 with the F16 codec decoder, Audio8 cloning with the F16 encoder.

The backend never destroyed its devices or its instance. Each device's own buffer type holds a `shared_ptr` to it, so `~vk_device_struct` never ran, and `vk_instance_t` has no destructor. The NVIDIA libraries register their exit handlers when `vkCreateInstance` loads them. At exit, `libEGL_nvidia`'s handler unmaps `libnvidia-eglcore` while a driver worker thread still runs code in it. Only `vkDestroyDevice` stops that thread. A crash-time signal handler showed the faulting pc in the unmapped `libnvidia-eglcore` range on that worker thread, right after the unmap.

A static destructor does not fix it. It is registered when `libqvac-speech-ggml-vulkan` loads, which is before the driver loads, so it runs after the driver's handlers. That version crashed in 20 of 20 runs. The fix registers the teardown with `atexit` after the driver is loaded.

Windows keeps the previous behaviour, because the exit handlers of a DLL run under the loader lock and Vulkan calls there can deadlock.

## Validation

| setup | runs | exit 0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jetson Orin, `parakeet --bench`, unpatched `speech@de1d0f5c` | 5 | 3 |
| Jetson Orin, `parakeet --bench`, this branch | 10 | 10 |
| Jetson Orin, `audio8-cli` LM F16 + codec decoder F16, this branch | 10 | 10 |

- Every Jetson run above completed its measurement. The Parakeet RTF is unchanged at 0.035.
- `ctest -R test-vulkan` passes 4/4 three times on the Jetson. It also passes on an RTX 5090 (proprietary driver) and on an AMD Raphael iGPU (RADV).
- `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` and `-o ADD` pass on the RTX 5090.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: two q8_0 `ADD` cases (`m=100,n=37,k=96`, modes 1 and 2) give NaN on the AMD iGPU. The unpatched `speech` tip shows the same result.

## Follow-up

- After the merge, the engine needs a `ggml-speech` registry cut at the merge commit on `speech` for the prebuilt addons. The weekly bench builds the `speech` head directly, so it picks this up on its next run.

> I reviewed the current head (`7231ceeb`) and found two teardown issues:
> 
>     1. **[P1] Destroy live Vulkan children before `vkDestroyDevice`.** `vk_device_struct::shutdown()` calls `device.destroy()` while a retained buffer still owns a VMA allocation, and a retained backend can still own fences, command pools, semaphores, descriptor pools, and events. The new `ggml_vk_cleanup()` guard then skips their cleanup when the backend is freed after teardown. This violates `VUID-vkDestroyDevice-device-05137` and makes the exit path dependent on driver behavior. Please release all live Vulkan children before destroying the device, while leaving their CPU wrappers safe to free later. See [shutdown](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml/blob/7231ceeb60e427f0a64a11b47320dc9c70916be4/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp#L1381), [late cleanup](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml/blob/7231ceeb60e427f0a64a11b47320dc9c70916be4/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp#L20143), and the [Vulkan requirement](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkDestroyDevice.html).
> 
>     2. **[P2] Keep `vk_instance` alive for cleanup handlers registered before dynamic backend loading.** With `GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON`, the test registers `free_retained` before `ggml_backend_load_all()` loads the Vulkan DSO. That DSO's nontrivial `vk_instance` static is constructed afterward, so its destructor runs before `free_retained` at exit. The latter still reaches `vk_instance.devices` through event and pinned-host-buffer frees. Leaking the registry device/context vectors does not preserve `vk_instance` itself, leaving those accesses outside its lifetime. Please retain the device directly in those resources or keep the lookup state alive through late cleanup. See [test registration](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml/blob/7231ceeb60e427f0a64a11b47320dc9c70916be4/tests/test-vulkan-teardown.cpp#L86), [`vk_instance`](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml/blob/7231ceeb60e427f0a64a11b47320dc9c70916be4/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp#L3372), [event free](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml/blob/7231ceeb60e427f0a64a11b47320dc9c70916be4/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp#L23693), and [host-buffer free](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml/blob/7231ceeb60e427f0a64a11b47320dc9c70916be4/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp#L20425).
> 
> 
> I attempted a local dynamic Vulkan build, but CMake configuration stopped because `SPIRV-HeadersConfig.cmake` is unavailable, so these are source-review findings rather than runtime reproductions.

Both fixed in 7cceb370.

P1, children destroyed after vkDestroyDevice. Each vk_device_struct now tracks its live backend contexts, events and VMA buffers. shutdown() cleans up the backends, destroys the event semaphores and events and releases the remaining buffers before it destroys the device; the CPU-side wrappers stay valid and a later free skips the Vulkan calls. ggml_vk_cleanup() also destroys the perf-logger query pool, which leaked before. P2, vk_instance lifetime with GGML_BACKEND_DL. vk_instance is never destroyed any more, so a cleanup handler registered before the Vulkan module loads can still free events and pinned host buffers through it.

issue.body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #410 in three parts.

**Jetson Orin Nano (`qvac-dev-linux-arm64`) lane, and the Strix Halo moves to `qvac-dev-strix-1`**

- `lib.sh` builds only the cmake targets of the selected families (plus `whisper-cli`), so a host whose `SKIP_FAMILIES` removes the MOSS families never compiles `moss-cli`.
- The cmake generator falls back to Unix Makefiles where ninja is missing (`qvac-dev-strix-1` has none).
- `EVICT_PAGE_CACHE=1` drops the model files from the page cache before every family, through a new `evict` subcommand of `prepare-derived.py` (`posix_fadvise` DONTNEED); the Jetson's CUDA allocations fail while the page cache is full.
- `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` in `config.env` is passed to the ggml and engine configures and is part of the build signature: the Jetson has no Vulkan SDK and no root, so SPIRV-Headers and Vulkan-Headers live under the bench home.
- `qvac-dev-strix-1` replaces `qvac-dev-strix-0` (the same hardware) as the one Strix Halo of the weekly set, under the plain name "Strix Halo"; the campaign's Strix Halo rows go with it.
- `config.example.env` and the skill's machine table document the Jetson and the Strix Halo.

**Speech Bench hub with task pages and per-machine dashboards, in the layout of the approved Speech Bench report**

- A hub page lists, per task (TTS and voice cloning, ASR, music), every machine with its models, backends and other engines, linking to that machine's task page, then the quality flags, the engines and how the bench runs. `build-landing.py` renders it from `hub.json`.
- The task pages follow the approved report's per-machine pages: one section per model with a horizontal speed chart per backend and input in engine colors, a details panel per chart (exact values, precision per row, the competitor ÷ QVAC time ratio with its qualifier, notes and sources) and what was not measured there, and why. `task_views.py` renders them from each machine's `runs.json` and `coverage.json`, with `dashboard/task.css`; `build-landing.py` embeds all of them in the hub as views reached at the hub's link plus `#<machine>-<task>` (for example `#dgx-spark-tts`), so they need no artifact of their own and are visible to everyone who can open the hub.
- One Dashboard artifact per machine runs the same page (`dashboard/index.html`, `app.js`, `app.css`, adapted from the approved report's dashboard script): an overview (status, a summary of the week, quality flags, which models ran on which backend, gaps, engines, rules), a tab per task with one section per model (a speed chart per backend and input; weekly charts hold QVAC's variants, campaign charts hold QVAC and transcribe.cpp, audio.cpp, LocalAI parakeet.cpp or acestep.cpp in engine colors, with details, time ratios and sources), a week-over-week line per backend, and a runs and coverage tab.
- `build-dashboard-data.py` writes per host the six files a dashboard reads (`runs`, `history`, `coverage`, `engines`, `machine`, `commentary`) and `hub.json`. Campaign rows keep their own build and date and never share a chart with weekly rows; a competitor without a ratio (OOM in the campaign) is a failed row, and a competitor row records its precision as not recorded instead of QVAC's quantization. Two campaign notes in `comparisons.json` that were cut at 400 characters are complete again. `engines.json` lists the engines, `dashboards.json` the links.
- The skill's publish step and the Monday refresh upload each machine's changed files to its dashboard and republish the hub.

**`fetch-registry.js`** discards a stale `.part` left by a stopped download, and downloads beside it when that file belongs to another user (the shared store is sticky).

## Additional information

- `test-desktop-weekly.sh` covers the selected-family target list, the generator fallback, the evict subcommand, the cmake prefixes in the build signature, the partial-download handling, the data builder, the hub and the task pages (27 checks pass; it also syntax-checks the dashboard script).
- Rehearsal runs with these tools are on the dashboards: DGX Spark 40/40, RTX 5090 60/60, Strix Halo 40/40, Mac mini 34/34, Jetson 34/39. The five Jetson Vulkan cells finish their measurement and then segfault at process exit on the Tegra driver (exit 139); the fix is tetherto/qvac-ext-ggml#148, after which the engine needs a ggml-speech registry cut.

issue.title: QVAC-27853 fix(vulkan): destroy devices and instance before driver unload
issue.body:
## Summary

- Destroy every Vulkan device and the instance from an `atexit` handler registered after the instance and each device are created, so it runs before the driver's own exit handlers.
- Split the `vk_device_struct` destructor into an idempotent `shutdown()` that waits for the device to go idle, skips a device that was never created, and destroys the VMA allocator only when it holds no allocations.
- After the teardown, buffers, pinned host memory and backend contexts freed later by the application skip their Vulkan calls.
- New `test-vulkan-teardown`: initialise `Vulkan0`, allocate and free a buffer, exit; a second ctest entry exits with the buffer still allocated.

## Error corrected

On the Jetson Orin (L4T 36.4, NVIDIA Tegra Vulkan driver 540.4.0, `nvgpu`), the speech CLIs finished their work, wrote their results, and then died with SIGSEGV at exit. The weekly bench therefore recorded 5 of the Jetson's 13 Vulkan cells as failed although their measurements were complete. Affected: Parakeet TDT, Parakeet Unified, Audio8 with the F16 codec decoder, Audio8 cloning with the F16 encoder.

The backend never destroyed its devices or its instance. Each device's own buffer type holds a `shared_ptr` to it, so `~vk_device_struct` never ran, and `vk_instance_t` has no destructor. The NVIDIA libraries register their exit handlers when `vkCreateInstance` loads them. At exit, `libEGL_nvidia`'s handler unmaps `libnvidia-eglcore` while a driver worker thread still runs code in it. Only `vkDestroyDevice` stops that thread. A crash-time signal handler showed the faulting pc in the unmapped `libnvidia-eglcore` range on that worker thread, right after the unmap.

A static destructor does not fix it. It is registered when `libqvac-speech-ggml-vulkan` loads, which is before the driver loads, so it runs after the driver's handlers. That version crashed in 20 of 20 runs. The fix registers the teardown with `atexit` after the driver is loaded.

Windows keeps the previous behaviour, because the exit handlers of a DLL run under the loader lock and Vulkan calls there can deadlock.

## Validation

| setup | runs | exit 0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jetson Orin, `parakeet --bench`, unpatched `speech@de1d0f5c` | 5 | 3 |
| Jetson Orin, `parakeet --bench`, this branch | 10 | 10 |
| Jetson Orin, `audio8-cli` LM F16 + codec decoder F16, this branch | 10 | 10 |

- Every Jetson run above completed its measurement. The Parakeet RTF is unchanged at 0.035.
- `ctest -R test-vulkan` passes 4/4 three times on the Jetson. It also passes on an RTX 5090 (proprietary driver) and on an AMD Raphael iGPU (RADV).
- `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` and `-o ADD` pass on the RTX 5090.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: two q8_0 `ADD` cases (`m=100,n=37,k=96`, modes 1 and 2) give NaN on the AMD iGPU. The unpatched `speech` tip shows the same result.

## Follow-up

- After the merge, the engine needs a `ggml-speech` registry cut at the merge commit on `speech` for the prebuilt addons. The weekly bench builds the `speech` head directly, so it picks this up on its next run.

## Overview

Adds `scripts/benchmarks/desktop-weekly/`, a cron-driven weekly benchmark of the speech engines on the team's shared Tailscale machines, independent of any developer machine. Each machine builds the current `master` of this repo and the `speech` head of qvac-ext-ggml for every backend it has, provisions the pinned models, runs the desktop matrix through the existing `scripts/benchmarks/run-family.sh`, and e-mails a Markdown report.

- **Machines and backends:** `qvac-dev-linux-x64` (RTX 5090: cpu, cuda, vulkan) and `qvac-dev-mac-arm64` (M3 Ultra: cpu, metal), Sunday 06:00 machine time. The run shares `/tmp/gpu-bench.lock` with the fabric-llm weekly bench (Saturday 00:00 Zurich on the Mac) and waits for that lock and for other users' GPU jobs before it starts.
- **Matrix (`families.json`, 20 families):** Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 Q8_0, Parakeet Unified English 0.6B Q8_0, TranscribePsy-250M-EU-sub Q8_0 (HuggingFace, pinned revision), Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B F16, Supertonic 3 Q8_0, the Audio8 TTS Preview grid (LM F16/Q8_0/Q4_0 x codec decoder F16/Q8_0) plus voice cloning with the F16 and Q8_0 codec encoders, MOSS-TTS v1.5 8.5B F16 and transformer-only Q8_0 plus F16 cloning, and ACE-Step 1.5 Turbo Q8_0 and Q4_K_M, SFT Q8_0 and Base Q4_K_M (the registry has no Base Q8_0; the row says so). The MOSS Q8_0 cut is not in the registry either and is requantized on the machine from the F16 backbone with `engines/tts/scripts/requantize-gguf.py`.
- **Report:** per backend, wall median with min and max, speed (audio seconds per wall second), peak RSS, GPU memory rise and peak from `nvidia-smi`, WER or TTS WER, observed backend; the machine (OS, kernel, CPU, GPU, driver, CUDA toolkit, Vulkan driver, toolchain versions); the engine and ggml commits, CUDA arch, registry client version, TTS scorer pin and every model file with size, sha256 and origin; every wall or RSS move over 5% since the previous finished run together with whether a pin changed; and the problem list. `summary.json` carries the same data for machines.
- **Delivery:** `send-report.py` (stdlib `smtplib`, config in `config.env`, secrets in files) mails the report with `report.md` and `summary.json` attached; a failed run mails a failure notice. `narrate.py` optionally asks Claude (`claude-opus-5-5` over plain HTTPS, the machines carry no SDK) for a ten-line narrative placed above the report.
- **Files:** `weekly.sh` + `lib.sh` (lock, source update, per-backend ggml and engine builds with a commit-pair marker, watchdog that kills a family's process group past its `timeout_minutes`, GPU sampler), `fetch-models.sh` + `fetch-registry.js` + `prepare-derived.py` (registry client, HuggingFace, repo fixtures, requantized and resampled files, one copy per machine in `MODELS_DIR` with `.sha256` and `.source` sidecars), `machine-info.sh`, `collect-pins.sh`, `summarize.py`, `report.py`, `install.sh` (deploys the tools and the crontab line), `config.example.env`, `README.md`.
- **Tests:** `test-desktop-weekly.sh` (script parsing, `families.json` completeness and provisioning consistency, lock, watchdog, build markers, run selection, offline model provisioning, machine and pin collection, install) and `test_*.py` for the Python pieces; the desktop benchmark workflow's plan job runs the suite with the existing driver self-check.
- **Docs:** README documentation table and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` benchmark coverage point at the new directory.
- **Claude side, modelled on qvac-fabric-llm.cpp#424:** `skills/speech-bench/SKILL.md` tells a Claude session how to deploy, run on demand, collect the summaries, rebuild the results page with `build-artifact.py` and update the weekly artifact in place, plus the coordination rules for the shared machines: the fabric-llm bench owns Saturday from 18:00 CET, the speech bench Sunday from 18:00 CET (about 6 to 7 hours), both hold `/tmp/gpu-bench.lock`, and nobody starts a run between Saturday 17:00 and Monday 02:00 CET. `install.sh` now defaults to Sunday 18:00 machine time. The first page, built from the 2026-11-03 smoke runs, is https://claude.ai/artifact/MAF5hDfMrpqbQ7Dsqmc8gY; a desktop scheduled task republishes it every Monday morning.

## Additional information

- Tested on the machines themselves on 2026-11-03 from a fresh `~/speech-bench` on each: `weekly.sh --quick --no-mail` (Parakeet TDT, Supertonic 3, one Audio8 pair, one timed iteration) finished `DONE` with 3 of 3 cells ok on `qvac-dev-linux-x64` (CUDA; 1.5 GiB, 0.9 GiB and 2.2 GiB of GPU memory rise recorded) and on `qvac-dev-mac-arm64` (Metal), including the source update, the registry fetch, the per-backend ggml and engine builds, the report, the changes section against the previous run and the lock release. A real-iteration run of the heavy families on the Mac (`moss-tts-f16`, `moss-tts-q8_0`, `moss-tts-clone-f16`, `acestep-turbo-q8_0`, `audio8-clone-enc-f16`, `transcribepsy`) finished 6 of 6 ok: the on-machine Q8_0 requantization of the 15.8 GiB backbone, the 24 kHz reference resample for cloning and the HuggingFace fetch with sha256 verification all went through the real path (MOSS F16 8.0 s and 18.2 GiB RSS, Q8_0 5.3 s and 12.1 GiB, ACE-Step Turbo 30 s render in 4.7 s, TranscribePsy 25 ms at 0% WER).
- The CPU and Vulkan backends, the e-mail delivery (no SMTP credentials exist yet) and the Claude narrative (no API key) were not exercised on the machines; `send-report.py --dry-run` and the unit tests cover their logic.
- `test-desktop-weekly.sh` passes locally (22 checks). A security and a correctness review pass with adversarial verification ran before this PR; the confirmed findings (executables under a shared folder, unverified SMTP TLS, `USER` unset under cron, failure mail attachments, stale rerun files, quick runs as baselines, provisioning keyed only on file names) are fixed.
- Not in the registry and therefore not exactly as requested: ACE-Step Base ships only as Q4_K_M; MOSS-TTS Q8_0 is a local requantization of the transformer blocks.
- Deployment state: the tools are installed under `~/speech-bench` on both machines (`MODELS_DIR` on the shared `qvac-speech/bench` folders) and the quick runs above are in `runs/`, but no crontab line is installed yet: on the Mac it is one `install.sh --hour 6` away; on the Linux box the full matrix needs about 60 GB for models and builds and the disk has 25 GB free, so old workspaces under `/home/zbigniew` have to go first.
- Results are read on the weekly artifact page (linked from the team channel's canvas), rebuilt every Monday by the speech-bench skill from the machines' summaries; e-mail delivery stays in the tree but is off unless `MAIL_TO` and the SMTP keys are set.
- `comparisons.json` carries the rows of the October 2026 QVAC speech engines campaign for the weekly models (transcribe.cpp, audio.cpp, LocalAI parakeet.cpp, acestep.cpp), shown under each task with qvac's RTF and the competitor-over-qvac time ratio per lane.
- The DGX Spark, Strix Halo and Mac mini run the same bench with per-machine settings (`config.example.env`): unified-memory sampler and sm_121a on the Spark, Vulkan plus `scheduler.sh` on the cron-less Strix, the `nsdate` clock shim and no MOSS on the 16 GB mini; `install.sh` falls back to `scheduler.sh` wherever the crontab write is refused.
- Mobile is out of scope here; the matrix and the report are host-agnostic so a Device Farm lane can reuse `families.json`, `summary.json` and `report.py`.

issue.title: ggml-webgpu: register no device when Dawn offers only its Null adapter
issue.body:
## Why

QVAC-27302 (tetherto/qvac-fabric-speech.cpp#390) runs the speech stack's WebGPU umbrella lane on a hosted runner with no Vulkan driver. There Dawn offers only its Null adapter, which accepts every feature and executes nothing. This backend registered a device on it, so whisper-cli aborted, the LavaSR enhancer produced non-finite samples and the VAD GPU test drifted. The ggml-speech port refuses that adapter (qvac-ext-ggml `2d3b497b`); this ports the check.

## What

- `ggml_backend_webgpu_reg`: an adapter whose `backendType` is `wgpu::BackendType::Null` registers no device, alongside the existing shader-f16 and implicit-sync checks.
- `tests/test-webgpu-null-adapter.cpp` (from the speech tree): every registered WebGPU device must compute a small add graph; `--expect-no-device` additionally requires zero devices and the CPU as best backend. The Linux `-no-driver` variant runs it with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` pointed at nothing.

## Verification

On qvac-dev-linux-x64 (RTX 5090, vcpkg Dawn): with the real Vulkan adapter the device computes; with the ICDs hidden no device registers and the CPU is the best backend. Before this change the hidden-driver run registered a Null device that did not compute (the speech lane's failure).

Neither new test sets this, so both exit with “no WebGPU backend registered” under the default environment. Set the opt-in environment variable for both tests, preserving the Vulkan overrides on the no-driver variant.
>

> 
> > Hiding Vulkan ICDs does not disable other GPU backends. In a Linux build with CUDA and WebGPU enabled, ggml_backend_load_all() also loads CUDA, and ggml_backend_init_best() correctly selects it. This makes the no-driver test fail even though WebGPU rejects the Null adapter correctly. Isolate this test to CPU and WebGPU registration before asserting that CPU is best.

The CMake comment says why the opt-in is there. The device-count check is unchanged; it only looks at the WebGPU registration and never depended on the other backends. The header comment spells out why hiding the Vulkan drivers alone is not enough.

issue.title: QVAC-27329 fix[api]: keep backend fields on streamed TTS stats and put the audiogen GPU fallback code on the wire
issue.body:
## Why

QVAC-27329. The Audio8 and ACE-Step SDK-vs-fabric measurements found two gaps in the result shapes rather than in performance:

- on the chunked TTS paths (`runStream()` / `runStreaming()`) the merged stats carried no `backendId` / `backendDevice`, so an SDK caller could not tell from `result.stats` where a streamed Audio8 synthesis ran;
- the SDK's `audioGen` stats dropped the addon's `gpuFallbackReason`.

## What

- **tts-ggml**: `mergeSentenceStreamStats` kept only `codecSidecarLoaded` and `codecOnCoreml` across chunks. It now keeps every backend field from the last chunk that reported it (`backendDevice`, `backendId`, `gpuUnsupported`, the LavaSR `enhancerBackend*` / `denoiserBackend*` pairs) plus the two codec flags, through one `LAST_REPORTED_STREAM_STATS` list. `lib/` regenerated with the pinned TypeScript; README, CHANGELOG (Unreleased) and a unit test added.
- **inference / sdk**: `audioGenStatsSchema` carries the raw `gpuFallbackReason` code next to `backendDevice` / `backendId`, so the `audioGen`, `audioEdit` and `audioUnderstand` stats mirror the addon on this too, and the run op uses that schema instead of a private extension. `diagnostics.fallback.reason` keeps naming a lost GPU as before. ACE-Step `metadata` was already forwarded since #5000. Contract `schema.json`, Kotlin and Python models regenerated; the `next` music-generation docs and the `audioGen()` JSDoc describe the fields.
- **inference / sdk, LavaSR denoiser pair** (review follow-up): `@qvac/tts-ggml` already reported `denoiserBackendDevice` / `denoiserBackendId`, but `collectTtsStats` forwarded only the enhancer pair and `ttsStatsSchema` did not declare them. Both now carry the pair, so the SDK `stats` say where the denoiser ran on batch and chunked runs alike; contract, Kotlin and Python models regenerated, and the `next` text-to-speech docs list the two fields.

## API

```ts
// SDK: tell a GPU fallback from a slow run
const run = audioGen({ modelId, caption: "warm cinematic piano" });
const stats = await run.stats;
stats?.backendDevice; // 0 CPU, 1 GPU, as before
stats?.gpuFallbackReason; // new: 0 none, 1 not requested, 2 no devices, 3 init failed
(await run.diagnostics)?.fallback?.reason; // "no-devices" | "init-failed", as before

// @qvac/tts-ggml: a chunked Audio8 run now says where it ran
const response = tts.runStream(longText, { voice: "Rohit" });
// ...after the stream ends:
response.stats.backendId; // 1 Metal, 2 CUDA, 3 Vulkan, ... (was absent on chunked runs)
response.stats.codecOnCoreml; // kept from the last chunk, as before
```

Additive on every surface: a caller that ignores the new field sees what it saw before.

- inference: `typecheck`, `lint`, `format`; `audio-gen-plugin`, `audio-gen-schemas` and `tts-stats` tests under bare (10/10, 37/37, 8/8); after the denoiser pair, `tts-stats` + `tts-schemas` under bare (102/102) and `contract:check` plus the Kotlin and Python generator `--check` runs clean

issue.title: perf(moss-sfx): run quantized matrices from ggml's repacked CPU layout
issue.body:
Stacked on #385 (base: `QVAC-27498/moss-sfx-q4_0`); retarget to `master` once it merges.

## Summary

On the CPU, MOSS-SoundEffect now runs its quantized text-encoder and DiT matrices from ggml-cpu's repacked layout (`CPU_REPACK`). That roughly halves CPU diffusion time on a Galaxy S25 (`q8_0` and `q4_0`) and on x86 (`q4_0`), with unchanged reference parity and memory.

## Changes

- `backend_selection`: `cpu_repack_buffer_type()` finds the CPU device's `CPU_REPACK` extra buffer type. `cpu_repack_runs_matmul()` asks the CPU device, through a zero-size candidate buffer, whether it runs a matrix product with a given weight in that buffer.
- `SfxModel`: on the CPU backend, quantized `text.blk.*` and `dit.*` matrices the probe accepts go to a second weight context and buffer. Everything else keeps the default buffer: the token table (read with `get_rows`), the VAE, the unquantized tensors, and matrices ggml cannot repack. Tensor lookup, streaming, the fit measurement and the scheduler's weight buffers cover both. `SfxLayout::packing` (`Automatic`, `Plain`) lets tests compare the layouts.
- `test-moss-sfx`: for `q8_0` and `q4_0` fixtures, the DiT and text matrices are packed exactly when ggml offers a layout for this processor, while the token table and VAE are not. Packed and default layouts give the same text context and DiT velocity, and the fit measures packed weights. Mutation-checked: disabling packing fails the `q4_0` placement checks on x86.
- Docs: SoundEffect engine notes (layout, measurements, why the LMs keep the default layout), the 4-bit and Hexagon sections' CPU numbers, both READMEs.

## Measurements

Diffusion for the two-step glass request (5 s, seed 7), two rounds in opposite orders:

| Machine | GGUF | Default layout | Repacked |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| Galaxy S25, 6 threads | `q8_0` | 137.8-140.7 s | 70.8-72.8 s |
| same | `q8_0`, DiT blocks `q4_0` | 145.8-146.2 s | 71.1-72.0 s |
| Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 8 threads | `q8_0`, DiT blocks `q4_0` | 30.6-30.9 s | 12.6-13.0 s |
| same | `q4_0` | 30.3-30.9 s | 12.6-12.9 s |

- `q8_0` has no x86 layout in ggml, so it is unchanged there.
- Peak RSS is unchanged.
- On the S25, text encoding drops from 177 ms to 90 ms.
- S25 CPU reference parity with packed weights: text 0.999545, DiT 0.999080 / 0.998967, eight steps 0.997490, the same as the default layout.
- The rendered audio differs from the default layout by summation order. The gap matches a CUDA render of the same request: waveform cosine 0.88 against 0.87 on a two-step clip.

Microbench on the S25 CPU (one `MUL_MAT`, 6 threads):

| Shape | Speedup, `q4_0` | Speedup, `q8_0` |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1500 rows, DiT matrices | 2.5-3.0x | 2.5-3.0x |
| 64 rows, 2048 x 6144 | 2.4x | 1.06x |
| 1 row, 4096 x 4096 and 4096 x 12288 | 0.41-0.66x | 0.42-0.78x |

The single-row products are why MOSS-TTS and MOSS-Speech decoding keep the default layout.

Tests:
- Host CPU ctest: 197/197.
- S25: `test-moss-sfx` passes, with both tiers packed on ARM. `test-moss-gpu hexagon` passes; its CPU reference now runs packed weights. CPU reference parity passes.

issue.title: QVAC-27329 fix[api]: keep backend fields on streamed TTS stats and put the audiogen GPU fallback code on the wire
issue.body:
## Why

QVAC-27329. The Audio8 and ACE-Step SDK-vs-fabric measurements found two gaps in the result shapes rather than in performance:

- on the chunked TTS paths (`runStream()` / `runStreaming()`) the merged stats carried no `backendId` / `backendDevice`, so an SDK caller could not tell from `result.stats` where a streamed Audio8 synthesis ran;
- the SDK's `audioGen` stats dropped the addon's `gpuFallbackReason`.

## What

- **tts-ggml**: `mergeSentenceStreamStats` kept only `codecSidecarLoaded` and `codecOnCoreml` across chunks. It now keeps every backend field from the last chunk that reported it (`backendDevice`, `backendId`, `gpuUnsupported`, the LavaSR `enhancerBackend*` / `denoiserBackend*` pairs) plus the two codec flags, through one `LAST_REPORTED_STREAM_STATS` list. `lib/` regenerated with the pinned TypeScript; README, CHANGELOG (Unreleased) and a unit test added.
- **inference / sdk**: `audioGenStatsSchema` carries the raw `gpuFallbackReason` code next to `backendDevice` / `backendId`, so the `audioGen`, `audioEdit` and `audioUnderstand` stats mirror the addon on this too, and the run op uses that schema instead of a private extension. `diagnostics.fallback.reason` keeps naming a lost GPU as before. ACE-Step `metadata` was already forwarded since #5000. Contract `schema.json`, Kotlin and Python models regenerated; the `next` music-generation docs and the `audioGen()` JSDoc describe the fields.
- **inference / sdk, LavaSR denoiser pair** (review follow-up): `@qvac/tts-ggml` already reported `denoiserBackendDevice` / `denoiserBackendId`, but `collectTtsStats` forwarded only the enhancer pair and `ttsStatsSchema` did not declare them. Both now carry the pair, so the SDK `stats` say where the denoiser ran on batch and chunked runs alike; contract, Kotlin and Python models regenerated, and the `next` text-to-speech docs list the two fields.

## API

```ts
// SDK: tell a GPU fallback from a slow run
const run = audioGen({ modelId, caption: "warm cinematic piano" });
const stats = await run.stats;
stats?.backendDevice; // 0 CPU, 1 GPU, as before
stats?.gpuFallbackReason; // new: 0 none, 1 not requested, 2 no devices, 3 init failed
(await run.diagnostics)?.fallback?.reason; // "no-devices" | "init-failed", as before

// @qvac/tts-ggml: a chunked Audio8 run now says where it ran
const response = tts.runStream(longText, { voice: "Rohit" });
// ...after the stream ends:
response.stats.backendId; // 1 Metal, 2 CUDA, 3 Vulkan, ... (was absent on chunked runs)
response.stats.codecOnCoreml; // kept from the last chunk, as before
```

Additive on every surface: a caller that ignores the new field sees what it saw before.

## Verified

- tts-ggml: `test/unit/sentence-stream.test.js` (9/9), `typecheck`, `lint:js`, `lint:ts`, `test:dts`
- inference: `typecheck`, `lint`, `format`; `audio-gen-plugin`, `audio-gen-schemas` and `tts-stats` tests under bare (10/10, 37/37, 8/8); after the denoiser pair, `tts-stats` + `tts-schemas` under bare (102/102) and `contract:check` plus the Kotlin and Python generator `--check` runs clean
- sdk: `test/audio-gen-client.test.ts` (18/18), `contract:export`, prettier and lunte on the touched files

Not run locally: the full sdk typecheck (its dev install is blocked on this machine by the Socket firewall on two dev-only transitive packages); CI covers it.

  (`ggml_conv_1d_dw_direct`, `ggml_norm_channel`, `ggml_pad_replicate_1d`,
  `ggml_bias_gelu`, `ggml_scale_residual` and the `_ct` variants). Signatures are
  identical, so this is a pure rename.
- Root CMake comment, README, docs (BUILD, ARCHITECTURE, UPSTREAM-SYNC,
  WHISPER-HEXAGON), engine guides, NOTICE and LICENSE name the fabric ggml.
  Historical records keep their commit-pinned provenance.
- CI workflows pin `GGML_REPO=qvac-fabric-llm.cpp` and a fixed `GGML_REF`
  instead of resolving the `speech` branch tip, and configure `ggml-src/ggml`.
- `setup-ggml.sh` (tts, parakeet) fetch the pinned fabric-llm commit into
  `ggml-src/` and link `ggml/` to its `ggml/` tree.
- Parakeet drops `PARAKEET_GGML_LIB_PREFIX`: the fabric ggml has no
  `GGML_LIB_OUTPUT_PREFIX` and names its DL backends `qvac-ggml-*` itself.

## Draft: blocked on fabric-llm ggml additions

The fabric ggml at `be6e387b` still lacks speech-branch APIs the engines use, so
whisper and the parakeet MOSS runtime do not link yet:

1. `ggml_backend_sched_get_host_size`, `ggml_backend_sched_get_work_size`,
   `ggml_backend_get_work_size`, `ggml_backend_graph_get_work_size` and
   `ggml_context_overhead` (MOSS transcribe memory fit).
2. CPU registry proc `"ggml_graph_plan"` (qvac-ext-ggml#92; Pocket TTS graph
   memory fit, `test-pocket-graph-memory` fails without it).
3. `ggml-hexagon.h` installed unconditionally with
   `ggml_backend_hexagon_runtime_info_v1` and the
   `ggml_backend_hexagon_get_runtime_info_v1` / `ggml_backend_hexagon_conv_taps_f32`
   procs (whisper-fit-memory.h, Pocket, Audio8).
4. Optional: `ggml_mul_mat_affine_v1` (Metal experiment behind
   `GGML_AFFINE_METAL_V1`).

## Verification

- Linux x64, CPU-only fabric ggml built standalone from `ggml/`: TTS and AudioGen
  build; 1748 of 1763 build steps succeed (the 15 failures are the gaps above);
  `ctest -L 'unit|fixture'` 174 of 194 pass (18 "Not Run" whisper/parakeet tests,
  `test-whisper-device-cli`, `test-pocket-graph-memory`).
- CUDA + Vulkan (RTX 5090) and Metal (M3 Ultra) builds and the GPU suites are
  running on the bench boxes; results to follow in this PR.
- Note for standalone ggml builds with Vulkan: fabric-llm keeps the VMA headers
  in the repository's `vendor/` directory, so the whole repository must be
  checked out (the workflows and docs do that).

issue.body:
## Summary

Part of QVAC-27302 (speech stack moving from `ggml-speech` to `qvac-fabric`). The
speech stack ships ggml's WebGPU backend as the opt-in `webgpu` feature of
`speech-cpp`; this gives `qvac-fabric` the same feature so `speech-cpp` can
forward to it once it depends on this port:

- `webgpu` feature: `GGML_WEBGPU=ON` plus the Python interpreter ggml-webgpu's
  shader embed needs; Dawn comes from microsoft/vcpkg's `dawn` port pinned by
  the consumer at 20260410.140140, the same contract as `ggml-speech[webgpu]`
  (fabric's ggml-webgpu uses the same Dawn callback API as the speech branch).
- Orthogonal to `gpu-backends`; under `GGML_BACKEND_DL` it becomes one more
  runtime-loaded module.
- `11259.2.0#1`, version database entry with the matching git-tree, baseline
  moved.

## Verification

`vcpkg install qvac-fabric[core,webgpu]` on x64-linux-release (qvac-dev-linux-x64,
this branch as overlay, `dawn[core,vulkan]` 20260410.140140 built from source):
exit 0; installs `libggml-webgpu.a` next to `libggml*.a` and `libwebgpu_dawn.a`;
`share/ggml/ggml-config.cmake` carries `GGML_WEBGPU "ON"`. Not yet built on
macOS (Dawn Metal) or with `gpu-backends` on; the speech-cpp consumer change
follows in a separate PR once the fabric ggml carries the remaining speech APIs
(tetherto/qvac-fabric-speech.cpp#387).
